conviction_note: A near-balanced name: a bar cut hard into the print (EPS consensus 0.35 -> 0.23 in 90 days, revenue consensus $415m = -6.2% reported, roughly -11.5% constant currency once a ~6% RMB tailwind is netted out), a crowded short (17.2m shares, 15.8 days to cover) and a stock at its 52-week low point up; a collapsing handset vertical, falling China car retail, a high Alibaba base, cautious management language and a name that sold its last beat point down. The findings sum to +0.3; p_up 52 on abs 4.0 gives +0.16. The bar is disputed (two Yahoo snapshots, $429m and $415m), so every bar-dependent finding is capped small.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus US$414.99m (8 analysts, low 404m, high 427.34m; year-ago 442.31m, -6.17%) and non-GAAP EPS US$0.23 (6 analysts, low 0.17, high 0.30; 90 days ago 0.35), Yahoo Finance analysis page read 2026-11-16, https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/WB/analysis/. A second, undated Yahoo snapshot surfaced in search showed 7 analysts at US$429.03m (-3%). The two disagree, and there is no company guide (Weibo gives no numeric guidance), so the bar is treated as disputed and the findings that depend on it are capped small. Q2 2026 for reference: revenue $453.8m vs ~$442.75-443.9m consensus, non-GAAP EPS $0.38 vs $0.36 (https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/wb).

next_guide.company_current_guide: none. Weibo gives no numeric guidance. On the Q2 call (2026-08-19) management said Q3 factors 'are expected to put some pressure on year-over-year advertising revenue growth', that the recovery in consumer demand will take longer, auto would stay strong, handsets were less optimistic, and e-commerce/food delivery would stay under pressure against the high base of last year's delivery price war (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/WB/Q22026).
next_guide.basis: There is no numeric guide to raise or cut. The qualitative Q4 tone will most likely stay cautious: handset shipments fell 15.4% y/y in Q3, China car retail fell 28% in September, and Q4 2025 is a +5% ad base with Alibaba quick-commerce spend in it. Against that, the street's Q4 -5.2% reported (about -11% cc with FX) already embeds a sharp decline.

findings.finding: The RMB averaged roughly 6.75-6.76/USD in Q3 2026 (July fixes 6.79-6.80, end-September 6.705) against about 7.16 in Q3 2025, a ~6% translation tailwind. Weibo's Q1 and Q2 2026 already showed a 6-point gap between reported and constant-currency growth (Q2: total +2% reported / -4% cc, ad -1% / -6% cc). So the $415m consensus (-6.2% reported) implies about -11.5% constant currency, roughly 7 points worse than Q2. Repeating Q2's cc rate would give revenue near $440m; even ad at -10% cc gives about $425-430m. A reported revenue beat of 2-4% is therefore likely, on a bar that is itself disputed ($429m in an older snapshot).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat revenue by ~2.5% and EPS by $0.02 and the stock fell 1.32% on the day, then made a new 12-month low two days later; Q1 2026 -2.97%. This name has not paid for reported-revenue beats that came with FX help.
findings.why_not_priced: The street can see FX as well as anyone, so the low bar may be deliberate: consistent with non-Alibaba ad at about -8% cc and Alibaba ad (Q3 2025: $45.5m, +112%) falling ~40%. If the market had priced a translation-driven beat, EPS revisions would not still be falling (3 down in 30 days) and the stock would not sit at its 52-week low. The beat is probably partly priced as 'consensus is stale', which is why it is sized small.

findings.finding: Expectations have been cut hard into the print. Non-GAAP EPS consensus for Q3 went from $0.35 (90 days ago) to $0.26 (60 and 30 days) to $0.23 now, a 40% sequential drop from Q2's $0.38 actual against a 22% seasonal Q2->Q3 step last year (0.54 -> 0.42). There were 3 downward EPS revisions in 30 days and 1 in 7 days. FY26 EPS went 1.42 -> 1.21. The stock is at its 52-week low, below the Morgan Stanley ($6.6) and BofA ($6.5) bear targets, after a Citi downgrade to Neutral on 2026-08-21.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print in the sample came off a bar this depressed. Q2 came in with EPS consensus at 0.36 (above the 0.33 whisper), beat it, and was sold -1.32%.
findings.why_not_priced: The revisions are themselves priced (the stock fell with them). The open question is whether a 0.23 bar, which implies a non-GAAP operating margin near the high teens against 28% in Q2, sits below what the company will print. If the market expected a clean clear, the stock would have bounced off the bear targets rather than breaking under them in the last 5 days (-5.7%).
findings.independence: Analyst actions: Morgan Stanley UW $6.6 (https://longbridge.com/news/288203232.md, 2026-06-01); Citi downgrade (https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/weibo-price-target-lowered-to-11-from-13-at-citi, per search, dated 2026-08-21 by Benzinga). findings.finding: The short is crowded and was rising into the print: 17,183,840 shares short at the 2026-10-30 settlement, up 781,971 from 10-15, with 15.82 days to cover on 1.09m ADV, roughly 20% of the ~86m ADS float. Any print that is not clearly worse than the cut bar gives covering a mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest was also 16-17m with DTC ~22 into the Q2 print (2026-08-14 settlement), and that print still went -1.32%. So the short has not squeezed on a beat before.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is public. What is not priced is how this float reacts if the release clears a bar that sits below Q2's run-rate. The sealed 25% annualised realised volatility and a dead option chain show nobody is paying for a move. The year-long persistence of the position (13-17m shares) suggests part of it is a structural hedge or arbitrage, which is why the size is moderate.

findings.finding: China's smartphone market shrank 15.4% y/y in Q3 2026 to about 57.9m units (IDC, 2026-10-13), accelerating from H1, as memory costs forced OEM price rises. Xiaomi was down 20.4% and OPPO and vivo fell sharply. Handsets are a core Weibo ad vertical that already declined in Q2, and management said on the Q2 call it was 'less optimistic' for Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 handset ad decline (flagged in the release) arrived alongside a -1.32% day. No separate line reaction is identifiable.
findings.why_not_priced: Management pre-warned on handsets, and the street's -11.5% cc implied bar plausibly already carries a weak handset vertical. What may not be priced is the depth: a 15% unit decline with OEM margin squeeze points to deeper ad cuts than 'less optimistic' implies. Net of the rest: auto, internet services and AI app promotion grew in Q2 and have to offset it.
findings.independence: Omdia: shipments -12%, lowest Q3 since 2013 (https://omdia.tech.informa.com/pr/2026/oct/mainland-china-smartphone-shipments-drop-to-lowest-q3-level-since-2013). This is an industry proxy; the company has not quantified handset ad revenue.

findings.finding: China passenger-car retail fell 28% y/y in September 2026 (CPCA final, 1.618m units) and 21.7% YTD, with NEV retail -16.7%. Automobile was the vertical Weibo said would show 'continued strength in the second half' on frequent NEV launches.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Auto advertising grew in Q2 2026 despite a weak 2026 car market (YTD retail already down), so retail volumes have not transmitted to Weibo's auto ad line so far.
findings.why_not_priced: Car makers fighting for share in a shrinking market often keep launch marketing high, so transmission to ad spend is ambiguous; it is filed small. If the market had priced an auto-ad cut, management's 'continued strength' would already have been questioned in analyst notes, and none found does so.
findings.independence: Steelorbis CPCA preliminary -24%: https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-news/latest-news/cpca-chinas-passenger-vehicle-retail-sales-down-24-in-september-2026-1482872.htm. Macro proxy, not confirmed by the company.

findings.finding: Alibaba, Weibo's largest single advertiser, described its September 2025 quarter as the peak of its quick-commerce investment and said intensity would fall significantly afterwards. Weibo's Alibaba ad revenue was $45.5m (+112%) in Q3 2025 against $39.2m (+10%, on AI app promotion) in Q2 2026. Weibo management said e-commerce would stay under pressure against the high base of last year's Q3-Q4 delivery price war.
findings.link: Alibaba is a related-party advertiser: about 10% of Weibo ad revenue (Q2 2026: $39.2m of $381.0m; Q3 2025: $45.5m of $375.4m), disclosed as a separate line in every Weibo release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025, when Alibaba ad more than doubled while non-Alibaba fell 13%: reaction not reliably sourced (only templated mirror pages). No measured reaction on this line.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: management flagged the base and the $415m consensus reconciles with Alibaba ad falling ~40%. The residual is that Alibaba's Qwen/AI-app promotion (which lifted Q2) may hold the line better than the consensus arithmetic assumes; the sign could flip, so it is sized small. Alibaba's own September-2026-quarter results were not found before this print.
findings.independence: Weibo Q3 2025 release for the base: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1595761/000110465925113392/tm2531299d1_ex99-1.htm. Weibo Q2 2026 call on e-commerce pressure: https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/WB/Q22026.

findings.finding: Management's only forward statement (Q2 call, 2026-08-19) was cautious: Q3 factors 'expected to put some pressure on year-over-year advertising revenue growth', the consumer recovery 'will take longer', and competition for ad budgets stays intense. The Q4 2025 base is +5% ad growth. With handset and car data deteriorating through the quarter, the Q4 commentary is more likely to extend the decline than to call a turn, against a street Q4 of $448.6m (-5.2% reported, about -11% cc).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the Q2 call, with the same cautious tone, the stock fell 1.32% and made a new 12-month low within two sessions; Citi downgraded the same week.
findings.why_not_priced: The street's Q4 already embeds a sharp cc decline, so a 'pressure continues' tone is mostly priced. The risk is a quantified statement (e.g. Q4 ad down double digits cc) or a margin warning, which this name has not given before. Shrunk for the crowded short.
findings.independence: Yahoo Q4 consensus: https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/WB/analysis/. Handset and auto data in findings 4 and 5 share this direction but are separate documents. The transcript is auto-generated and partly garbled.

findings.finding: Weibo has a US$200m buyback authorised through 2026-12-31, about 13% of the ~$1.48bn market cap at $6.04 (245.67m shares), funded from cash. Cash and short-term investments were $2.64bn at June 30, above the market cap. Execution to date is undisclosed. A Q3 release reporting heavy repurchases at 52-week lows, or a renewal, would be a support. The annual dividend ($0.61 in 2026, -26%) is set with Q4 results in March, outside this window.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The program was announced 2025-12-31 alongside the Sina Section 238 judgment; no reaction to a buyback disclosure in an earnings release is measured.
findings.why_not_priced: Execution is unknown. GuruFocus shows zero buyback through Q1 2026, which, if accurate, means the authorisation has been idle. A disclosed acceleration would be new information, and an idle program is no change, so the size is small and positive.
findings.independence: Cash figure: https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/wb (Q2 release summary). Buyback yield 0.00% as of 2026-08-12: https://www.gurufocus.com/term/buyback-yield/MEX:WB N (cuts against execution).

outside_window.finding: Sina, Weibo's controlling shareholder, lost a Section 238 Cayman appraisal judgment over its 2021 privatization; enforcement is stayed pending appeal. Any pressure on Sina to extract cash (dividends) or sell Weibo shares resolves with the appeal, not with this print.

The annual dividend (2026: $0.61/ADS, ~$150m, -26% y/y) is declared with Q4 results in March. A 10% trailing yield at spot makes the 2027 dividend the next capital-return catalyst, outside this window.

baseline_tension: The baseline has no skew and only a contaminated history. What I found leans slightly against the run-down (low bar, crowded short, stock under the bear targets), but the rebuilt reaction history (two sold prints) and the deteriorating handset and auto data cut the other way, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (bar disputed: $415m vs $429m, two Yahoo snapshots, no company guide): FX/consensus-beat finding capped from +0.8 to +0.4; expectations finding trimmed from +1.0 to +0.8.
Rule 1 (this name sold its Q2 beat, -1.32%): no second cut to finding 1 (already capped once); p_up moved from 54 to 52.
Rule 7 (crowded short, DTC 15.8): negatives shrunk once: handset -0.5 -> -0.4, Alibaba -0.5 -> -0.4, next guide -0.6 -> -0.5.

Rule 5 (macro proxy not confirmed by the company): auto-retail finding -0.3 -> -0.2; short-interest finding +0.9 -> +0.8 because the position has been persistent all year (partly structural); buyback +0.3 -> +0.2 because execution is unconfirmed.
History rule (FPI 6-K matcher contamination): the reaction base was rebuilt from the two confirmed earnings days (2026-05-28, 2026-08-19); this left reaction_history at -0.4 and abs_move_pct at 4.0.
